rubrics.rubric: Does the vendor payment integrity audit correctly identify that CHK-1402 ($1,847.50 to ABC Supplies on 02/09/2024) has no matching AP invoice for that exact amount, and investigate it as a potential partial payment against AP10003 ($4,433.05, status Partial)?
criterion: The response must flag CHK-1402 ($1,847.50) as a discrepancy because no AP invoice in the Q1 2024 USD subledger matches this exact amount

The response must reference the six ABC Supplies invoices: AP10003 ($4,433.05, Partial), AP10758 ($2,204.28, Paid), AP10362 ($2,005.72, Paid), AP10498 ($597.75, Open), AP10155 ($249.12, Open), AP10260 ($3,084.27, Paid)
The most plausible explanation—a partial payment on AP10003 (status 'Partial'), leaving a remaining balance of approximately $2,585.55 ($4,433.05 − $1,847.50)—must be noted
The response should identify this as a vendor payment integrity exception requiring investigation

rubrics.rubric: Does the vendor audit identify that AP10274 (Fast Travel, $970.98) is marked 'Open' with no PaidDate in the AP subledger, but bank reference EFT-2210 shows the payment cleared on 02/10/2024, constituting an AP status error?
criterion: The response must identify the status inconsistency for AP10274: the bank statement shows EFT-2210 clearing $970.98 to Fast Travel Services on 02/10/2024
The AP subledger records AP10274 ($970.98, Fast Travel, invoice date 2024-02-10, due 2024-03-11) as 'Open' with no PaidDate, which is an AP subledger data integrity error
The response must state that the status should be corrected to 'Paid' with PaidDate 2024-02-10
This discrepancy must appear in the exceptions log as requiring correction

rubrics.rubric: Does the vendor payment cross-reference correctly match at least 5 of the 6 matchable vendor-related bank withdrawals to their corresponding AP invoices, and flag CHK-1402 ($1,847.50) as unmatched?
criterion: The response must cross-reference 7 vendor-related bank withdrawals (6 checks + 1 EFT) against the AP subledger

At least 5 of the 6 correct matches must be identified: (1) CHK-1401 $2,204.28 → AP10758 (ABC Supplies, Paid); (2) CHK-1403 $2,005.72 → AP10362 (ABC Supplies, Paid); (3) CHK-1404 $3,133.53 → AP10452 (Global Office, Paid); (4) CHK-1405 $2,302.71 → AP10108 (BluePrints, Paid); (5) CHK-1406 $4,543.11 → AP10581 (Global Office, Paid); (6) EFT-2210 $970.98 → AP10274 (Fast Travel, status discrepancy)
CHK-1402 ($1,847.50) must be flagged as having no matching AP invoice

rubrics.rubric: Does the AP aging schedule correctly classify the open/partial Q1 2024 USD invoices into aging buckets as of March 31, 2024, with AP10003 ($4,433.05), AP10454 ($1,074.85), and AP10234 ($2,206.77) in the 31-60 days past due bucket?
criterion: The response must age all 6 Q1 2024 USD invoices with Open or Partial status as of March 31, 2024

When aging from due date: AP10003 (due 2024-02-07, 53 days past due → 31-60 days), AP10454 (due 2024-02-10, 50 days past due → 31-60 days), AP10234 (due 2024-02-23, 37 days past due → 31-60 days) must be in the 31-60 day bucket
The remaining invoices—AP10498 (due 2024-03-06, 25 days), AP10155 (due 2024-03-24, 7 days), and AP10485 (due 2024-03-25, 6 days)—should fall in the Current/0-30 days bucket

If aging from invoice date instead (yielding 61-90 day bucket for the three oldest), that is acceptable if consistently applied, but the three oldest invoices must be classified in a more aged bucket than the newer ones

rubrics.rubric: Does the Schedule C expense mapping correctly assign COGS (Account 5000, $4,421.20) to Line 4, Travel Expense (Account 5010, $7,534.42) to Line 24a, and Payroll Expense (Account 6000) to Line 26?
criterion: Account 5000 COGS totaling $4,421.20 (7 entries: $383.71 + $254.62 + $822.42 + $242.28 + $726.03 + $1,835.61 + $156.53) must map to Schedule C Line 4 (Cost of goods sold)
Account 5010 Travel Expense totaling $7,534.42 (8 entries: $283.45 + $200.91 + $753.12 + $292.84 + $1,330.42 + $1,450.58 + $1,814.27 + $1,408.83) must map to Schedule C Line 24a (Travel)

Account 6000 Payroll Expense must map to Schedule C Line 26 (Wages/less employment credits); the GL-only total is $5,861.39 (8 entries), though the response may reconcile this against the $51,000 in bank payroll disbursements
The amounts and line assignments must all be correct

rubrics.rubric: Does the reconciliation identify the significant discrepancy between bank payroll disbursements ($51,000.00 for six payments of $8,500 each) and the GL Payroll Expense account entries ($5,861.39 total from eight smaller entries), and investigate or explain this $45,138.61 gap?
criterion: The bank statement shows six payroll direct deposits of $8,500.00 each (ACH-PR0115, PR0131, PR0215, PR0229, PR0315, PR0331) totaling $51,000.00, while the GL Account 6000 Payroll Expense contains eight entries totaling only $5,861.39
The response must identify the $45,138.61 discrepancy between bank payroll disbursements and GL payroll expense entries

The response must investigate possible explanations: (a) GL entries are supplemental payroll costs (taxes, benefits, adjustments) while $51,000 cash disbursements were recorded elsewhere or not at all; (b) payroll was accrued to a liability account; (c) systemic failure to record payroll cash transactions in the GL
This is the largest single discrepancy in the reconciliation and must be prominently flagged

rubrics.rubric: Does the reconciliation investigate DEP-0129 ($4,127.26, described as 'Customer Payment net of fees' on 01/29/2024) and analyze the fee deduction by comparing it to the closest GL revenue entry or other deposits?
criterion: The response must investigate DEP-0129 ($4,127.26) which is described as 'net of fees'

The analysis should compare this to nearby GL entries to determine the gross amount and fee deducted, such as GL000434 ($4,172.26 on 01/29, Account 4000) yielding a fee of $45.00, or GL001447 ($4,741.00 on 01/26, Account 4000) yielding a fee of $613.74
The response must note the ambiguity and explain that the fee should be recorded as an expense (e.g., Account 5020 Bank Service Charges or a payment processing fee account)
Simply ignoring the 'net of fees' notation or failing to investigate the implied fee deduction fails this criterion

rubrics.rubric: Does the reconciliation note the date discrepancy between CHK-1401 (bank clearance date 01/10/2024) and AP10758 (PaidDate listed as 02/09/2024) for the $2,204.28 payment to ABC Supplies?
criterion: The response must identify that CHK-1401 for $2,204.28 to ABC Supplies cleared the bank on 01/10/2024, but the matching AP record AP10758 lists a PaidDate of 2024-02-09—a 30-day discrepancy

The response should investigate possible causes: the check may have been issued earlier than the bank clearance date, the AP PaidDate may reflect when internal books were updated rather than bank processing, or there may be a data entry error
This discrepancy should appear in the exceptions log

rubrics.rubric: Does the exceptions log (Deliverable 3) contain at least 8 distinct discrepancies with proper Exception_ID, Source_File, Reference, Description, Amount, Resolution, and Status fields?
criterion: The Q1_2024_Reconciliation_Exceptions.csv must contain at least 8 distinct exceptions covering major discrepancies: (1) CHK-1402 unmatched payment ($1,847.50); (2) AP10274/EFT-2210 status discrepancy ($970.98); (3) CHK-1401/AP10758 date mismatch ($2,204.28); (4) DEP-0129 net-of-fees ambiguity ($4,127.26); (5) NSF returned check ($750.00); (6) Missing GL entries for rent ($9,600); (7) Missing GL entries for auto loan payments ($3,750); (8) Payroll GL vs. bank discrepancy ($45,138.61 gap)

Each exception must have all required columns: Exception_ID (unique identifier), Source_File (which file the discrepancy was found in), Reference (transaction reference number), Description (clear explanation), Amount (dollar amount), Resolution (action taken or recommended), and Status (Resolved or Unresolved)

rubrics.rubric: Does the Schedule C Draft worksheet (Sheet 4 of the Reconciliation Workbook) correctly replicate the Schedule C structure with Part I (Income) including Line 1 gross receipts of $40,557.62 and Part II (Expenses) with line-level amounts that tie back to the expense summary?
criterion: Sheet 4 must replicate the IRS Schedule C structure with Part I Income showing Line 1 Gross receipts (combined Sales Revenue $23,318.47 + Online Sales $17,239.15 = $40,557.62), Line 4 COGS ($4,421.20), Line 5 Gross Profit ($36,136.42), Line 6 Other income (Interest Income $37.56), and Line 7 Gross income ($36,173.98)

Part II Expenses must include amounts for Line 15 (Insurance), Line 20b (Rent $9,600.00), Line 24a (Travel $7,534.42), Line 25 (Utilities $1,275.00), Line 26 (Wages), and Line 27a (Other expenses—bank charges $105.00)
The amounts must be internally consistent and tie back to the Q1_2024_Schedule_C_Expense_Summary.csv
